1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 f5 3.exf5.strategy: Takes the pawn and keeps it: Black's gambit hopes to pull White's e-pawn away from the centre, but White simply gains a pawn. The open diagonals Black has created also weaken the e6 and e5 squares and the king, so White can develop calmly and let Black's compensation fade.

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 f5 3.exf5 Nh6.strategy: Aims to win the pawn back with the knight, which attacks f5 from the edge of the board. It is slow and awkward: the knight does little else there, and White, a pawn up, can simply go on developing while Black's king is still short of cover on the e8-h5 diagonal.
1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 f5 3.exf5 Nh6.name: Sicilian Defence: Double-Dutch Gambit
